item.title: Client-Focused Freelance Marketplace Website
item.description:
250-750 CAD | I’m launching a web platform that lets clients post a task, collect offers from vetted freelancers, and release payment only after they approve the finished work. Phase-one is strictly client-facing, so every screen, flow, and call-to-action must speak to someone who wants to hire talent—freelancer self-service can wait until later iterations.
Your assignment covers the full build:
• UX/UI: clean, modern, responsive pages for account creation, project posting (budget, timeline, brief), and an offers dashboard where incoming proposals can be compared at a glance. • Core logic: secure login, project database, real-time offer feed, basic messaging thread per job, and an escrow-style payment trigger that releases funds only on client approval. • Admin tools: moderation panel to view projects, inject offers manually when needed, and handle dispute or refund actions. • Tech stack: I’m open, though a popular combo such as React or Vue on the front end with Node, Laravel, or Django on the back adds long-term flexibility. Please suggest what you do best and why. • Compliance: GDPR-ready data handling, Stripe or PayPal integration, HTTPS, and a straightforward privacy/terms generator.
Acceptance criteria 1. A new client, using only a browser, can register, post a job, and see at least one test offer without staff intervention. 2. Funds held in escrow cannot be released until the “Approve work” button is clicked. 3. Pages load in under three seconds on standard 4G per Lighthouse tests. 4. All copy and UI elements are English-ready and stored for easy localisation later.
Hand over clean, documented code in a Git repo plus a brief deployment guide (Docker or standard VPS). Once these boxes are ticked, milestones close and payment is cleared.

item.title: Build a Modern, Responsive Business Website with Digital Product Sales
item.description:
250-750 USD | Project Overview
I’m looking for an experienced web developer to design and develop a modern, professional, and fully responsive website for my business.
The website should showcase my business, explain our services, and allow visitors to purchase digital products directly from the site, including downloadable files, digital resources, and online courses.
I want a clean, user-friendly website that looks professional, performs well, and makes managing content and digital products easy without requiring coding knowledge.
Key Requirements
1. Modern Website Design - Clean, professional, and visually appealing design. - Consistent branding that highlights the business and its services. - Fully responsive layout for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. - Easy navigation and user-friendly experience.
2. Digital Product E-Commerce Functionality - Dedicated product pages with descriptions, images, and pricing. - Shopping cart and secure checkout functionality. - Support for selling downloadable digital files and online courses. - Automatic delivery of purchased files or course access. - Basic license management or restricted access to purchased products. - Integration with reliable payment gateways.
**3. Content Management System (CMS) - Easy-to-use admin dashboard. - Ability to add, edit, and remove website pages and content. - Ability to upload and manage digital products. - No coding required for routine website updates.
4. Performance and SEO - Fast-loading and performance-optimized pages. - Mobile-first development. - SEO-friendly website structure and basic on-page SEO. - Google Analytics and Google Search Console integration.
5. Website Launch and Support - Domain connection and website deployment. - Basic testing across desktop and mobile devices. - Testing of the complete purchase and digital delivery process. - Admin login credentials. - A short video tutorial or walkthrough explaining how to manage the website and add new products.
Preferred Technologies
I’m flexible with the technology stack, but I prefer established platforms such as:
- WordPress + WooCommerce - Shopify - Other suitable platforms for digital product sales.
Feel free to recommend an alternative solution if it provides the required functionality, security, performance, and ease of management.
Project Deliverables
The completed project should include:
1. A fully functional, modern, responsive business website. 2. Digital product listings with working shopping cart and checkout. 3. Secure payment processing and automatic digital product delivery. 4. A user-friendly CMS and admin dashboard. 5. Basic SEO configuration and Google Analytics/Search Console setup. 6. Domain connection and live website deployment. 7. Admin credentials and a short management tutorial.
Acceptance Criteria
The project will be considered complete when: - The website passes a usability review on desktop and mobile. - A test purchase of a digital product works successfully. - Purchased digital products are delivered automatically or course access is granted immediately. - All major website features work as expected. - I receive administrator access and instructions for managing the website independently.
What I’m Looking For
I’m looking for a reliable developer with experience in website design, WordPress, WooCommerce, and digital product e-commerce.
Please include the following in your proposal:
- Examples of similar websites you have developed. - Your recommended platform and why you recommend it. - Your estimated delivery time. - A brief explanation of how you would approach this project.
My goal is to build a professional, scalable website that showcases my business and provides a smooth experience for customers purchasing digital products.
I look forward to reviewing your proposals!

item.title: Revamp HospoFix WordPress Website
item.description:
200-250 AUD | Hi,
Below is the brief for updating the HospoFix website. It outlines the website structure, content, services and functionality required.
HOSPOFIX – WEBSITE DEVELOPMENT BRIEF
1. Website Update & Brand Direction
Update the existing HospoFix WordPress website, retaining current functionality where practical. Avoid unnecessary plugins, platforms or additional features.
Brand positioning:
HospoFix – Practical Support. Better Operations.
Helping hospitality businesses run better through practical operational advice, systems and hands-on support.
The website should look professional, modern and welcoming, with a practical, knowledgeable and approachable tone. Avoid making it feel overly corporate.
2. Website Navigation
Main navigation:
- Home - About - Services (dropdown with all seven services) - Insights & News - Who We Help - Contact
Include a prominent Discuss Your Business or Make an Enquiry button. The logo should link to the homepage. FAQs can initially be accessed through the footer.
Navigation must work across desktop, tablet and mobile.
3. Homepage – Vision & Content
The homepage must introduce HospoFix, explain what makes us different and encourage hospitality business owners to explore our services or make an enquiry.
It should not simply be a list of services. Visitors need to understand who we are, what problems we solve and how we help businesses improve.
Our message:
HospoFix provides practical operational support to hospitality businesses. We help owners identify problems, improve day-to-day operations, control costs, strengthen systems and processes, and run their businesses more efficiently and profitably.
Our focus is on the everyday running of hospitality businesses – what happens behind the scenes and on the floor. We help owners make practical improvements that work in the real world. We are not a restaurant design, renovation or fit-out consultancy.
Suggested homepage layout:
1. Opening section: Headline, short introduction and enquiry button.
Headline: Helping Hospitality Businesses Run Better.
Supporting text: From improving rostering and controlling costs to strengthening systems and everyday operations, HospoFix provides practical hospitality support to help your business work smarter, operate more efficiently and improve profitability.
2. What We Do: Explain our practical approach to identifying operational challenges and finding workable solutions. 3. Our Services: Introduce all seven services with short descriptions and links to their individual pages. 4. How We Work: Explain our two flexible support options – Advice & Guidance and Hands-On Operational Support. 5. Who We Help: Introduce the hospitality businesses we support, including restaurants, cafes, pubs, bars, independent operators, hospitality groups and new venue owners. 6. Why HospoFix: Highlight our practical approach, operational focus and understanding of the pressures of running a hospitality business. 7. Enquiry section: Encourage visitors to discuss their business challenges and find out how we can help.
Include affordability messaging:
"You don't have to commit to more support than you need. Professional hospitality expertise may be more affordable than you think."
The homepage should build confidence, feel welcoming and make it easy for potential clients to get in touch, even if they are unsure what support they need.
4. About HospoFix
Create an About page explaining what HospoFix does, our hospitality experience and practical approach, and our focus on improving day-to-day operations.
Highlight how we help businesses improve systems, processes, people, costs, efficiency and profitability. Keep the focus on operational support rather than general hospitality project consulting.
5. Services – Seven Dedicated Pages
Each service should have its own page under the Services dropdown. Explain who it is for, what it involves, the problems it addresses and how HospoFix can help.
1. Operational Health Check
Best for owners wanting to identify operational problems and improve efficiency.
We review day-to-day operations, including front-of-house workflow, order processes, kitchen service and team efficiency. We identify bottlenecks and provide a practical action plan to help the venue run more smoothly.
2. Roster Stabilisation
Best for venues experiencing labour cost pressures, inconsistent rostering or staffing issues.
We review staffing structures, rosters and labour costs, identify inefficiencies and help develop better rostering and labour management processes to control costs and improve service.
3. Compliance Review
Best for businesses wanting to identify compliance gaps and potential risks.
We review relevant workplace and hospitality requirements, including award rates, food safety programs, local council permits and business registration requirements. We identify potential issues and provide guidance on areas needing attention.
4. Margin Evaluation
Best for owners wanting to understand where profits are being lost through costs, waste, supplier pricing or inaccurate costing.
We review supplier invoices, menu pricing, recipe costs and cost of goods sold (COGS). We identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve margins and make better purchasing and pricing decisions.
5. Operational Handbook
Best for venues needing clear procedures and consistent standards for managers and staff.
We develop practical documents tailored to the venue, such as front-of-house and kitchen checklists, staff procedures, supervisor guidelines, labour management processes and preparation systems.
6. Smart Technology Integrations
Best for owners wanting to improve efficiency and simplify service through technology.
We assess technology needs and help plan workflows around tools such as table booking systems, POS systems, QR ordering and payment solutions, making systems more efficient for staff and customers.
7. New Operator Launchpad – Coming Soon
Best for first-time hospitality owners or couples entering the industry who want practical guidance when establishing their business.
We provide guidance and training around the everyday requirements of running a hospitality venue, including operational fundamentals, team processes and practical on-the-floor support.
Clearly mark this service as Coming Soon, not currently available.
6. Flexible Support Options
Explain that services can be delivered at different levels depending on each client's needs.
Advice & Guidance: Operational reviews, assessments, identifying inefficiencies, labour cost analysis, rostering recommendations, systems advice, profitability opportunities and action plans. The client generally implements the recommendations.
Hands-On Operational Support: Working alongside owners, managers and staff to implement improvements, establish procedures, improve rostering and labour management, introduce systems and provide ongoing operational support.
These are flexible options, not fixed packages. Clients may need advice, hands-on assistance or a combination of both.
Pricing depends on the scope of work, time commitment and level of involvement. Do not publish fixed prices on the website.
7. Who We Help
Include a section or page covering:
- Restaurants and cafes - Pubs and bars - Independent hospitality operators - Hospitality groups - New and prospective venue owners
Link relevant services and include enquiry prompts.
8. Insights & News – Blog
Set up an Insights & News section using the existing WordPress blog functionality.
Include:
- Blog landing page with article cards, featured images, titles, dates and excerpts. - Individual article pages, categories and browsing of older posts. - Links to relevant services. - Mobile-friendly design.
I plan to publish approximately every 6–8 weeks. Topics may include labour costs, rostering, restaurant profitability, POS systems, food costs, margins, waste, opening a venue, hospitality technology and relevant Australian industry news.
I need to manage articles myself through WordPress, including writing and editing, uploading images, selecting categories, adding Rank Math SEO titles and descriptions, previewing, publishing and scheduling.
The developer is responsible for the blog design and templates, not ongoing article writing.
9. FAQs & Footer
Create an FAQ page with expandable questions and answers. I will supply the content separately.
Footer links should include About, all seven services, Insights & News, Who We Help, FAQs, contact details and social media links.
10. Technical Requirements
- Retain existing WordPress functionality where practical. - Responsive design for desktop, tablet and mobile. - Consistent branding and professional presentation. - Good loading speed and performance. - Basic on-page SEO using Rank Math where appropriate. - Easy content management. - Avoid unnecessary plugins and additional costs.
11. Handover & Future Development
On completion, provide:
- All updated pages and service pages. - Blog layout and article templates. - A short demonstration of how to publish and manage articles. - Desktop and mobile testing. - Basic instructions for updating content. - Details of ongoing maintenance and any additional costs.
Allow room for future additions such as case studies, downloadable resources, checklists, templates and industry research. These are not part of the initial development scope.
Please provide a breakdown of the proposed work and costs before proceeding, and identify anything outside the agreed scope.
Overall goal: Create a professional website that clearly positions HospoFix as a practical hospitality operations consultancy, explains our services and makes it easy for potential clients to understand how we can help and get in touch.
Thanks.

item.title: Build a Website for 59-Second AI Videos With Buy Buttons
item.description:
250-750 USD | **Update for bidders**
Thanks to everyone who bid. I received nearly 300 bids early on and have now received several hundred. I’m working through them and will follow up directly with shortlisted bidders. There’s no need to submit a new bid unless you’re updating your scope or price.
The full website will be a subscription service with **three subscription tiers**. Please include recurring billing and the ability for me to configure each tier’s pricing, features, and usage limits in the full website quote. I’ll decide the final prices and limits later. Please keep the fixed pilot price, full website quote, ongoing costs, and later mobile app estimate separate.
I want a website that helps people sell their books and products on social media without having to make or post the videos themselves. A user adds a book or product, connects their social accounts, and sets a schedule. The website creates the videos and posts them with a buy button for the exact item featured.
**How it should work**
1. **Add a book or product.** For a book, the user uploads a Word or PDF manuscript and the cover. For a product, such as a shirt, they enter a description and upload any photos they want used. In either case, they provide the exact product listing or purchase link.
2. **Connect accounts and set a schedule.** Each user connects their own YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok accounts. They choose where to post and set the days, times, and time zone for each account.
3. **Create the video.** The website uses AI to write the script and create the narration, visuals, and captions. The entire finished video must be **59 seconds or less**, including the closing sales message. If it’s too long, the website shortens it and makes a new version automatically.
4. **Post automatically or ask for approval first.** In automatic mode, videos go live on schedule without the user having to review them or finish the upload. In approval mode, the user can preview and approve a video or tap **Generate a New Video** if they don’t like it. The replacement promotes the same item and must be approved before it goes live. If the scheduled time passes without approval, hold the post.
5. **Put a buy button on every post.** Viewers should be able to tap a buy button or product tag on the post itself and go straight to the exact book or product. A link in the bio or a picture of a button doesn’t count.
**User dashboard**
Show the **next five videos in the posting queue**, including what each video promotes, where and when it will post, and whether it’s awaiting approval. Let users preview, approve, or regenerate a video from the queue. Show the schedule for each connected account and let users edit it.
**If a platform can’t do this**
Explain in your bid which part won’t work and why. Suggest the simplest alternative that keeps the process mostly hands-off. Spell out what the user has to do once, what they’d have to do for each video, and any extra costs. Don’t publish without a buy button unless the user has chosen that alternative.
**Please break your bid into three separate prices**
1. **Pilot:** Use one book and one product, such as a shirt. Show which platforms can publish a scheduled video automatically with a working buy button that takes a viewer to the correct listing. Also demonstrate the dashboard, how a rejected video gets replaced, and that an unapproved video stays unpublished in approval mode. 2. **Full website:** Build the browser-based version first. It should work on desktop, iPad, and phone without a download. This is the version I plan to launch first. 3. **Mobile app later:** Give me a separate price for an iPhone and iPad app after the website is built. If you can also build an Android version, price that separately. Explain how customers would keep the same login, products, connected accounts, and schedules.
Include a timeline for each phase and list ongoing costs separately. **The mobile app is for pricing only right now. It won’t be awarded as part of the website project and will be listed on Freelancer separately.**

item.title: Custom Unifi Captive Portal Integration
item.description:
20-250 GBP | I already have a working Unifi network, a cPanel hosting account, and an HTML landing page with a separate Terms & Conditions file. What I need is the glue that turns these assets into a fully-functional External Portal Server for Unifi.
Scenario • When a guest joins the WiFi they must see my branded splash page with links/Logos to Instagram/Facebook & Google Reviews. • They simply tick “I accept the terms and conditions” (no forms, no vouchers). • Once the terms are accepted, the portal should hand authentication back to the Unifi controller and immediately redirect the guest to our chosen social-media page.
Your task • Adapt my existing HTML (landing + T&C) so it meets Unifi’s External Captive Portal requirements: proper form fields, required POST/GET variables, redirect handling, and success state. • Deploy the finished code on my cPanel space and confirm it communicates correctly with the Unifi controller (USG / UDM firmware current). • Provide any controller-side settings I must enter (portal URL, redirect URL, guest control options) so I can reproduce the setup later.
Acceptance 1. Guests connect, see the splash, accept, and are online in one click. 2. Browser is redirected to the specified social-media URL. 3. No certificate warnings or mixed-content errors appear. 4. Source files and any instructions are delivered in a tidy folder.
HTML, CSS, PHP (or lightweight Python) solutions are fine as long as they run on standard cPanel hosting.

item.title: Redesign Kreol Magazine’s WordPress Experience
item.description:
250-750 GBP | Kreol Magazine Website Redesign: Brief for a Freelance Designer About the project
Examples for reference: https://www.wanderlustmagazine.com/ https://www.essence.com/
We want a fresh, modern, image led website for International Kreol Magazine at kreolmagazine.com, keeping our existing articles and shop. Kreol Magazine celebrates Creole culture, heritage, identity and diaspora communities worldwide, from Louisiana and Haiti to Seychelles, Mauritius and La Réunion. It is published in print and online by Rila Publications Ltd, London. The new site should feel as polished as a leading travel magazine and as warm and community centred as a leading culture magazine. Our readers should land on the homepage and immediately see beautiful stories, the latest issue, and a clear way to subscribe or support us. Our goals 1. Look current, confident and premium on phone and desktop. 2. Make our newest stories and the latest print issue easy to find. 3. Grow newsletter sign ups, subscriptions, shop sales and advertising enquiries. 4. Be simple for our small team to update every week without a developer. The current site and what must change The current site runs on WordPress with the Valenti theme and a WooCommerce shop. The content is rich, but the design looks dated and crowded. What we see today What we want instead Homepage is a long stack of about 12 similar category blocks A short, curated homepage with a clear lead story and a few strong sections Very long menus with many empty or placeholder links A simple menu of six to eight items, every link working Placeholder images and repeated stories Every story has a strong image; no duplicates Most articles show no publication date Date, author and category on every story Latest issue is easy to miss Latest print issue promoted near the top, with Buy and Subscribe buttons Only YouTube is linked Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn and others linked in header and footer No visible newsletter sign up Newsletter sign up on the homepage, in articles and in the footer Old content (some from 2014 to 2022) sits prominently Fresh content leads; older pieces live in an archive Keep: our domain, all existing articles and their web addresses, the shop, the Support Us page, the Advertise page and our YouTube videos. Inspiration: what to borrow Please study these two sites. We are not copying them; we want the same quality, adapted to Kreol's own identity. Site What we like and want to borrow Wanderlust Large, full width travel photography. A clean header with logo, search, menu and a Subscribe button. A strong magazine issue block with the cover, "View latest issue" and "Subscribe". Themed sections such as "Destination of the month" and "Editors' choice". A destinations area with trending places. Clearly labelled sponsored content. Essence Warm, people centred storytelling that celebrates culture and community. Portraits and event photography at the heart of the page. A "Trending" strip and a "Latest stories" feed with times shown. Video interviews as a regular format. A short one line summary under every headline. A clear "In the magazine" section for print features. For Kreol, this translates to: Wanderlust's beauty and structure for our travel and destination content, combined with Essence's warmth for our profiles, music, food and community stories. New menu structure The main menu should have seven items, plus Search and a Subscribe button on the right. Submenus stay short. Menu item What sits under it People Profiles, Interviews, Three Wishes Culture History and Heritage, Art, Music, Books and Authors, Creole Inventors Travel Destinations (Louisiana, Seychelles, Mauritius, Haiti, La Réunion and others), Festivals and Events Food Recipes, Food Stories Living Wellbeing, Education, Sport Videos All video interviews and event films The Magazine Latest Issue, Back Issues, Shop, Subscribe, Support Us The footer should hold About Us, From the Editor, The Meaning of Creole, Advertise with Us, Contact, Terms, Privacy, Cookies, social links, the newsletter sign up and our company details. Homepage layout, section by section The homepage should be short and curated, in this order from top to bottom: 1. Header: Kreol logo, menu, search, social icons and a Subscribe button. 2. Lead story: one large full width photograph with headline, one line summary and category. 3. Trending now: a strip of four to six recent stories. 4. Latest issue: the cover of the newest print issue, its main cover lines, and Buy, Subscribe and View Issue buttons. 5. People: three or four profile portraits, our signature content. 6. Destination of the month: one Creole place (for example Louisiana or Seychelles) with three or four stories. 7. Videos: a row of video interviews and event films with clear titles. 8. Culture, Food and Music: a mixed grid of stories, each with image, headline and one line summary. 9. Newsletter sign up: a simple box asking for name and email. 10. Partners and advertising: a tasteful space for sponsors, clearly labelled, and a link to Advertise with Us. 11. Footer. Article pages should have a large lead image, headline, summary, author, date, easy reading text, pull quotes, image galleries, share buttons, related stories at the end and a newsletter sign up. Look and feel The site should feel elegant, warm, proud and international: a premium magazine, not a blog. • Photography first: large, high quality images of people, places, music and food. • Colours: a clean white or warm cream background with our signature deep red (hex 8B0000) as the accent colour, plus one or two warm supporting tones inspired by the Creole world (ocean, sunset, earth). • Typography: an elegant serif for headlines and reading text (similar in spirit to Georgia), paired with a clean sans serif for menus, labels and buttons. • Space: generous white space and fewer, larger items rather than crowded grids. • Logo: keep the Kreol name; the designer may suggest a light refresh if helpful. • Mobile first: most readers will visit on a phone, so every page must look excellent on mobile. Please show us two or three mood boards or homepage design options before building. Features and technical requirements Must have • Stay on WordPress (unless the designer makes a strong case otherwise), with a modern, well supported theme or custom design. • Move every existing article, image and video across, keeping the same web addresses so Google rankings are not lost; any changed addresses must redirect. • Keep the WooCommerce shop for print issues, back issues and Support Us, with GBP and USD prices. • Newsletter sign up connected to a mailing service (for example Mailchimp). • Fast loading, secure (https everywhere), and good search engine set up. • Accessible to all readers: readable text sizes, good colour contrast, image descriptions. • Cookie notice and privacy pages that meet UK rules. • Clear categories, tags, authors and dates on all stories. • Easy for our team to publish a story, change the lead story and update the latest issue without technical help. Nice to have • A digital edition of each issue (flip book or PDF reader) for subscribers. • A Destinations map showing Creole places around the world. • A Read Aloud (audio) button on articles. • Simple advertising spaces we can sell to partners. • Basic visitor statistics (for example Google Analytics). Deliverables, timeline and what to send with a quote We expect the project to take about 10 to 12 weeks in five stages, with our approval at the end of each one. 1. Discovery (week 1 to 2): review the current site and content, agree the plan. 2. Design (week 3 to 5): mood boards, then homepage, article page and shop page designs for mobile and desktop. 3. Build (week 6 to 9): build the site on a test address, move all content across. 4. Testing (week 10): we check every page on phone and computer; fixes made. 5. Launch and training (week 11 to 12): go live, set up redirects, train our team, and provide a short written how to guide. After launch: please include 30 days of free bug fixes and quote separately for monthly support and maintenance. Please send with your quote • Links to two or three magazine or editorial websites you have built. • Your total price, broken down by stage. • Your proposed timeline and availability. • Who will do the work (design, build, or both). • Your suggested theme or platform, and why.
